key_insight: Disentangle local (mask-focused) and global (scene/temporal) control so the model only computes heavy operations where edits occur, enabling high-quality video inpainting with much lower latency and cost.
problem_solved: Pre-trained video foundation models waste computation by processing full video context even for small, localized edits; EditCtrl addresses this inefficiency to enable fast, scalable generative video editing.
method: Disentangled controllers: a local pathway that concentrates computation and high-resolution reconstruction inside inpainting masks, and a global pathway that preserves scene context and temporal consistency.
Mask-aware sparse computation and attention routing so only affected frames/patches receive expensive processing, while the global controller supplies lightweight contextual guidance.
Plug-and-play integration with pre-trained video foundation models to retain generation quality while greatly reducing FLOPs and latency for localized edits.
impact: Makes interactive, real-time generative video editing practical by cutting unnecessary computation for sparse edits—beneficial for content creators, product prototypes, and large-scale video pipelines.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: two parallel tracks (Local Controller vs Global Controller) showing where heavy computation is applied only inside masks.
Before / Mask / After triptych: a sample frame with the edit mask and the edited result to show localized change with preserved context.
Bar/line chart: compute cost or latency vs. mask size comparing full-frame baseline and EditCtrl to highlight efficiency gains.
Timeline view: temporal consistency illustration showing smooth edits across multiple consecutive frames (global controller effect).
paper_title: EditCtrl: Disentangled Local and Global Control for Real-Time Generative Video Editing
paper_authors: Yehonathan Litman, Shikun Liu, Dario Seyb, Nicholas Milef, Yang Zhou
